345158.title: Exact-value conjecture for Ryser's function
345158.statement:
For integers $r$ and $t$ with $2\leq t\leq r$, let an $(r,t)$-graph be an $r$-uniform, $r$-partite, $t$-intersecting hypergraph, and define

$$
\operatorname{Ryser}(r,t)=\max\{\tau(\mathcal H):\mathcal H\text{ is an }(r,t)\text{-graph}\},
$$

where $\tau(\mathcal H)$ is the cover number. **Bustamante--Stein and Király--Tóthmérész's exact-value conjecture.** For all $2\leq t\leq r$,

$$
\operatorname{Ryser}(r,t)=\left\lfloor\frac{r-t}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The paper proves this value in the range $r\leq 3t-1$ and establishes further partial results, but the formula remains conjectural in general.

345188.title: The unlabelled bridge-addable connectivity conjecture
345188.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a class of graphs, let $\tilde{\mathcal A}_n$ be the set of unlabelled graphs in $\mathcal A$ on $n$ vertices, and let $\tilde{R}_n \in_u \tilde{\mathcal A}$ denote a graph sampled uniformly from $\tilde{\mathcal A}_n$. A graph class is **bridge-addable** if adding an edge between vertices in distinct components preserves membership. **Unlabelled bridge-addable connectivity conjecture.** There is a $\delta>0$ such that, if $\mathcal A$ is bridge-addable, then

$$
\mathbb P(\tilde{R}_n \text{ is connected})\geq\delta
$$

for each $n$. This asks for a uniform positive lower bound on connectivity in the unlabelled setting; the source notes that little was known about this case and refers to a theorem below that bears on the question.

345562.title: Nonexistence of infinity-regular subrows in the Kolakoski sequence
345562.statement: Let $S$ be the Kolakoski sequence and let $\mathcal{SR}(S)$ denote its set of subrows. An **$\infty$-regular subrow** is a subrow that is $k$-regular for every $k$. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no $\infty$-regular subrows in $\mathcal{SR}(S)$. This conjecture would imply the stated consequence in Theorem 1; it arises from the apparent increase in the number of independent conditions required for a finite word to be $k$-regular as $k$ grows.

345642.title: Conjecture on coprime splitter sets for purely singular perfect splittings
345642.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $B[-k_1,k_2](m)$ be a perfect purely singular splitter set with splitter set $S$. Thus $S$ is the set of multipliers defining the splitting of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_m$.

**Coprime splitter conjecture.** Let $k_1, k_2$ be integers with $0 \le k_1 \leq k_2$ and $k_1 + k_2\ge 4$. If there exists a purely singular perfect $B[-k_1,k_2](m)$ set with splitter set $S$, then

$$
\gcd(s,m)=1\qquad\text{for all }s\in S.
$$

The source proposes this conjecture as implying both the Zhang–Ge conjecture and Woldar's conjecture. It is not resolved in the supplied text.

345726.title: The independence-number-two conjecture for prescribed roots
345726.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph, and let $calpha(D)$ denote its independence number. An **out-branching** rooted at $s$ is denoted by $B_s^+$, and an **in-branching** rooted at $t$ is denoted by $B_t^-$. The branchings are **arc-disjoint** if they have no common arcs. A digraph is $3$-arc-strong if its arc-connectivity is at least $3$.

**Prescribed-roots conjecture.** Every $3$-arc-strong digraph $D=(V,A)$ with $calpha(D)=2$ has a pair of arc-disjoint branchings $B_s^+,B_t^-$ for every choice of $s,t\ro V$.

This strengthens the preceding independence-number-two claim by requiring arbitrary, possibly different, roots and is presented as an open conjecture in the source.

351504.title: The kernel existence conjecture for colored quasi-transitive digraphs
351504.statement:
Let $D$ be an $H$-colored $r$-quasi-transitive digraph with $r\geq 2$. A **$(k,H)$-kernel** is a kernel of $D$ satisfying the $(k,H)$-reachability conditions defined for $H$-colored digraphs.

**Kernel existence conjecture.** For every $k\geq r+2$, the digraph $D$ has a $(k,H)$-kernel.

This conjecture extends the preceding results for the relevant classes of quasi-transitive digraphs. Its general validity for all $H$-colored $r$-quasi-transitive digraphs and all $k\geq r+2$ remains open.

351804.title: The extremal $A_\alpha$ spectral radius conjecture for non-strongly connected digraphs
351804.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}_n^m$ be the class of digraphs under consideration, let $G”$ denote the specific extremal digraph constructed in the preceding results, and let $A_\alpha$ be the $A_\alpha$ matrix of a digraph, with spectral radius $\rho_\alpha$. **Extremal $A_\alpha$ spectral radius conjecture.** For every digraph in $\mathcal{G}_n^m$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1)$, $G”$ has maximal $A_\alpha$ spectral radius among all digraphs in $\mathcal{G}_n^m$. The preceding theorem establishes this conclusion only for $\alpha\in\left[\frac{d_{G^*}^+(v_1)}{d_{G^*}^+(v_1)+n-m-n_1+1},1\right)$ or $\alpha=0$; the conjecture proposes that it holds throughout $[0,1)$.

352072.title: Gvozdenović–Laurent bound for the copositive stability-number hierarchy
352072.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)$ be its order-$r$ copositive hierarchy bound, and let $S^\perp$ denote the vertices adjacent to or equal to a stable set $S$. For every stable set $S\subseteq V$ with $|S|=r$, the graph $G\setminus S^\perp$ is obtained by deleting $S^\perp$. The **Gvozdenović–Laurent bound.** For every $r\geq1$,

$$
\vartheta^{(r)}(G)\leq r+\max_{S\subseteq V,\ S\text{ stable},\ |S|=r}\vartheta^{(0)}(G\setminus S^\perp).
$$

The source states that this conjecture implies the main convergence conjecture. Its general validity is not established in the supplied text.

352363.title: Reid–Wu–Zhou's cocircuit conjecture for minimally connected matroids
352363.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid, and let $k$ be a positive integer. The matroid $M$ is **minimally $k$-connected** if it is $k$-connected and $M\setminus e$ is not $k$-connected for every element $e$ of $M$.

**Reid–Wu–Zhou's cocircuit conjecture.** If $M$ is a minimally $k$-connected matroid with $|E(M)| \ge 2(k-1)$, then $M$ has a cocircuit of size $k$.

Murty and Wong proved the conjecture for $k\leq 3$. Reid, Wu, and Zhou proved it for $k=4$ with the unique exception of the $9$-element matroid $N_9$, and disproved it for every $k\geq 5$ by constructing examples with $2k+1$ elements. They conjectured the displayed restriction on the ground-set size might still suffice, but this remains open.

352370.title: Uniform bound conjecture for balanced spanning tree factorizations
352370.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be a **$k$-multiple tree**, meaning that the edge set of $G$ is the disjoint union of the edge sets of spanning trees $(T_1,\ldots,T_k)$. Such an ordered collection is a **spanning tree factorization** of $G$. Write $d_{T_i}(v)$ for the degree of $v$ in $T_i$. **Uniform bound conjecture.** There is an integer $c$ such that every $k$-multiple tree $G$ has a spanning tree factorization $(T_1,\ldots,T_k)$ such that

$$
|d_{T_i}(v)-d_{T_j}(v)|\leq c
$$

for all $v\in V(G)$ and $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. This asks whether the bound in the solved conjecture can be chosen independently of $k$ and remains open according to the source.

352396.title: Hickman–Wright's Kakeya set conjecture over finite cyclic rings
352396.statement:
Let $N,n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $S\subseteq (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^n$ be a Kakeya set, meaning that $S$ contains a line in every direction in $\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{n-1}$. **Hickman–Wright's Kakeya set conjecture.** For all $\epsilon>0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $C_{n,\epsilon}$ such that every Kakeya set $S\subset (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^n$ satisfies

$$
|S|\geq C_{n,\epsilon}N^{n-\epsilon}.
$$

The conjecture gives a near-full-dimensional lower bound for Kakeya sets over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, uniformly for general $N$. The source states that this conjecture is resolved in the paper, so its status is solved.

352492.title: Bounded hyperplane order in Green–Sanders examples
352492.statement: For a prime $p$, let $\mathrm{GS}(n,p)$ denote the Green–Sanders example, and let an $m$-**HOP$_2$** mean the paper's $m$-th order hyperplane order property. **Green–Sanders HOP2 conjecture.** For every prime $p$, there is $m\geq 1$ such that $\mathrm{GS}(n,p)$ has no $m$-HOP$_2$. This generalizes the established statement for $p=3$, where the example has $3$-HOP$_2$ but no $4$-HOP$_2$; no general resolution is stated.

352585.title: The 3-zero-sum partition property conjecture
352585.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite Abelian group, and let $I(\Gamma)$ denote its set of involutions. **The 3-zero-sum partition property conjecture.** If $|I(\Gamma)|>1$, then $\Gamma$ has the 3-Zero-Sum Partition Property: for every partition $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ of $|\Gamma|-1$ with $m_i\geq 3$ for all $i$, the nonzero elements of $\Gamma$ can be partitioned into subsets of these respective sizes, each having sum zero. The conjecture is proved in the paper for groups of order $2^n$; the other even-order cases with more than one involution remain open.

352587.title: The equal-sum partition conjecture for cyclic groups of order $2^n$
352587.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_m$ be a cyclic group of order $m=2^n$. Let $t$ and $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^t m_i=m-1,
$$

with $m_1\geq 1$ and $m_i\geq 2$ for $2\leq i\leq t$. **Equal-sum partition conjecture.** There exists $\mu\in\mathbb{Z}_m$ such that the nonzero elements of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ can be partitioned into disjoint subsets $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ with $|S_i|=m_i$ and

$$
\sum_{s\in S_i}s=\mu
$$

for every $i$, $1\leq i\leq t$. This is presented as an equivalent formulation of the complete multipartite distance-magic conjecture, whose status is not separately resolved in the source.

352628.title: 3-dimensional Dinitz Conjecture
352628.statement: A **partial Latin cube** of order $n$ is an $n\times n\times n$ array of symbols in which no symbol appears more than once in any slice. For every triple $(i,j,k)$ with $1\leq i,j,k\leq n$, let $S_{ijk}$ be a set of size $n^2$. **3-dimensional Dinitz Conjecture.** There exists a partial Latin cube $(a_{ijk})_{1\leq i,j,k\leq n}$ such that $a_{ijk}\in S_{ijk}$ for every triple $(i,j,k)$. This is presented as the three-dimensional analogue of the Dinitz conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution.

352856.title: Hartsfield's antimagic conjecture for trees
352856.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree. An **antimagic labeling** of $T$ is a bijection $f:E(T)\to\{1,\ldots,|E(T)|\}$ such that the vertex weights

$$
w(v)=\sum_{e\in E(v)}f(e)
$$

are distinct for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(T)$. **Hartsfield's tree antimagic conjecture.** Every tree other than $K_2$ is antimagic, meaning that it admits an antimagic labeling. This is the tree-specific conjecture stated alongside the general connected-graph conjecture; its status is not resolved by the supplied source context.

358587.title: Bašić et al.'s existence conjecture for circulant nut graphs of degree divisible by four
358587.statement: A **circulant nut graph** is a circulant graph whose adjacency matrix has a one-dimensional null space spanned by a full vector. Let $d$ be a degree satisfying $d \equiv_4 0$, and let $n$ be even with $n \ge d+4$. **Bašić et al.'s conjecture.** For every such $d$ and $n$, there exists a circulant nut graph of order $n$ and degree $d$. The conjecture gives a sufficient existence condition matching the necessary condition for vertex-transitive nut graphs in the case that the degree is divisible by four; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

359400.title: Oxley's circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture
359400.statement: For a matroid $M$, a **circuit-cocircuit intersection (CCI)** is a subset of its ground set that is the intersection of a circuit and a cocircuit. **Oxley's circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture.** A matroid with a CCI of size $k\ge4$ has a CCI of size $k-2$. Oxley implicitly observed the conjecture for $k=6$, and Kingan and Lemos proved it for regular matroids. The paper establishes it for every CCI of size $k\le7$; the general case remains open.

365570.title: Tannenbaum's zero-sum partition conjecture for Abelian groups
365570.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite Abelian group of order $m$, and let $I(\Gamma)$ be its set of involutions. Assume $|I(\Gamma)|>1$, and put

$$
R=\Gamma\setminus\bigl(I(\Gamma)\cup\{0\}\bigr).
$$

**Tannenbaum's zero-sum partition conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$ and every integer partition $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ of $m-1$, with $m_i\geq 2$ for every $i\in[1,|R|/2]$ and $m_i\geq 3$ for every $i\in[|R|/2+1,t]$, there is a subset partition $\{S_i\}_{i=1}^t$ of $\Gamma^*=\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S_i|=m_i$ and

$$
\sum_{s\in S_i}s=0
$$

for every $i\in[1,t]$. Cichacz and Suchan disproved the conjecture in general; it holds in the cases covered by the cited $2$-ZSPP and elementary $2$-group theorems.

371727.title: Bounded clique-width from bounded chordless-cycle subgraphs
371727.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let ${\cal P}=(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ be a **monotone partition** of $V(G)$ into cliques. The **box graph** $b(G;{\cal P})$ has a chordless cycle $A_{i_1}\dots A_{i_c}A_{i_1}$ for which the induced subgraph on the corresponding parts has bounded clique-width. **The bounded-cycle clique-width conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that, if for every chordless cycle $A_{i_1}\dots A_{i_c}A_{i_1}$ of $b(G;{\cal P})$ one has

$$
\operatorname{cwd}(G[A_{i_1}\cup\dots\cup A_{i_c}])\leq x,
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{cwd}(G)\leq f(k,x).
$$

This would extend the forest case, where the clique-width is bounded by $k+1$, to monotone partitions whose box graphs may contain cycles. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
